sections.html:
Jeffersontown, known as J-town, is a city inside Louisville Metro, so a sale involves both city and Jefferson County rules. The city bills its own real estate tax and licenses its own businesses, while the Jefferson County Property Valuation Administrator sets the assessment. Sellers who forget the city bill are the ones most often surprised at closing.

The city counted 28,474 residents in 2020 on about 10.6 square miles, a density near 2,700 people per square mile, and the July 2025 estimate is 29,193. It is fully urban and densely built, with 12,083 households and a 5.0% housing vacancy rate in 2020.

The middle owner-occupied value is $250,700, and 70.1% of households own. Mortgage holders carry about $1,601 a month in housing costs at the median, and renters pay $1,320. The median household earns $81,506. Residents 65 and older are 21.9% of the population, so downsizing and estate sales are common.

Bluegrass Commerce Park, which now covers more than 1,800 acres with roughly 850 businesses and 38,000 jobs, makes Jeffersontown the third-largest employment center in Kentucky. Average travel time to work is 21.5 minutes, so the park's jobs are a natural selling point for nearby houses. If you are selling after a downsizing or an estate, expect a retail buyer to want a cleared, updated house, and plan for the cost of clearing it.

The city mails its own real estate bill during the first week of October. A 2% discount applies if the bill is paid by October 31, the base amount is due December 31, and on January 1 a one-time 6% penalty is added with 6% annual interest on the unpaid balance.

Jeffersontown city real estate tax dates
DateWhat happens
First week of OctoberBills mailed to the last owner on file
October 31Last day for the 2% discount
December 31Base amount due
January 1Delinquent, 6% penalty, interest begins
May 1 after the tax yearCity lien filed in county records

Tax still unpaid on May 1 after the tax year brings a lien filed with the Jefferson County Clerk. Mortgage companies get copies of every bill, so ask your lender whether the tax comes out of escrow. At a sale, the seller typically pays the buyer a prorated share covering the seller's months of ownership.

The deed tax in KRS 142.050 falls on the grantor at 50 cents per $500 of value, rounded up. The county clerk takes it when the deed is recorded.

The Jefferson County PVA assesses real property at fair cash value. Owners 65 and older qualify for the homestead exemption, and owners classified as totally disabled qualify for the disability exemption, both applied for through the PVA. To contest a value, attend the 13-day open inspection period that begins the first Monday of May and meet with the PVA before an appeal is filed with the clerk. For plot information on a lot, call the Jefferson County Clerk's office at (502) 574-5700.

sections.h2: Permits that can affect a sale
sections.html:
The city's Department of Permitting and Code Enforcement issues building, trade and demolition permits. A permit is required to construct, enlarge, alter (including interior demolition), move or change the use of a building, and to install an in-ground pool. Ask your inspector or lender what proof of past permits they will want. If your house has a recent addition, gather the permit and inspection sign-off before listing.

  • Fences up to 4 feet in front or street-side yards, 8 feet for solid fences and 6 feet for chain link in rear or side yards, need no city permit. Corner lots must keep sight lines clear.
  • Home occupations are limited to 10% of the home, two deliveries a day and one non-resident employee.
  • In-ground pools need Metro Health Department approval first, then a city permit, and a four-foot fence with a self-latching gate.
  • Businesses operating in the city register and pay a $75 annual fee within 10 days of starting, and every contractor and subcontractor must hold an active city business license before work begins.

sections.h2: Local taxes for landlords and owners
sections.html:
Jeffersontown has no net profit tax, gross receipts tax, income tax, personal property tax or intangible tax. What it does charge is narrower.

  • A 1% occupational withholding tax on gross wages earned for work performed in the city, remitted by employers each quarter on April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31.
  • The $75 annual business license for operating businesses, with exemptions for nonprofit 501(c) groups, banks chartered by the state and governmental agencies.
  • Late occupational tax carries a 5% monthly penalty, capped at 25% of the tax, plus 1% monthly interest.

If you rent the house and are unsure whether a registration applies, ask the Revenue Department at city hall before the sale so the account can be closed cleanly.

Your closing agent will pull together the lender payoff, the city and county tax figures and any lien search results. Ask the city's Revenue Department for its number as well, since the city bill is separate from the county's and easy to miss. Proceeds are what is left after those payoffs, the deed tax and the proration.

You sign the deed, the county clerk collects the tax and records it, and the buyer's funds are released. A cash buyer can usually close faster because no lender appraisal or underwriting has to be scheduled.

Before you list, walk the lot and the house with a permit checklist in hand. An unpermitted pool, a finished basement or a deck can slow a financed buyer, since the lender's appraiser and the buyer's inspector both ask about it. Find out early, and either close the permit or price the gap into the offer you accept.

Start with a paper trail: the deed, a lender payoff, the city and county tax bills and permit records. Then weigh the routes. A listing works for an updated house when you can wait for loan approval. A cash sale fits a house still full of belongings, with deferred repairs or an open estate. An investor can buy a rental and keep the tenant. Request written closing costs and tax prorations from every buyer before you pick one.

faqs.q: Does Jeffersontown bill its own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The city bills a real estate tax separately from Louisville Metro and the county, with bills mailed in early October and a 2% discount through October 31. Ask the Revenue Department at city hall, 10416 Watterson Trail, for a payoff before closing.

faqs.q: What if I miss the Jeffersontown real estate tax deadline?
faqs.a: A bill unpaid on January 1 draws a one-time 6% penalty and 6% annual interest, and a lien is filed if it stays unpaid on May 1 of the following year. A lien is released when tax, penalty and interest are paid in full.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax on a Jeffersontown sale?
faqs.a: The seller, as grantor. KRS 142.050 sets the tax at 50 cents per $500 of value.

faqs.q: Can a Jeffersontown homeowner age 65 or older get a tax exemption?
faqs.a: Yes. The city offers a homestead exemption for owners 65 and older and a disability exemption for owners classified as totally disabled. Both are applied for through the Jefferson County PVA.

faqs.q: Should I add a fence or pool before selling in Jeffersontown?
faqs.a: A fence within the height limits needs no city permit, but an in-ground pool needs Metro Health Department approval and a city permit. Start neither project unless it can be finished and inspected before the closing.
